planting.note: Set out container-grown plants in spring in moist, well-drained soil with some relief from the harshest afternoon sun.

directions: Chirimen is a dwarf Hinoki cypress named for its tightly congested, crinkled sprays of foliage, which resemble the texture of crinkled chirimen crepe fabric rather than the flat, fan-like sprays typical of the species. It grows slowly into a dense, irregular mound and holds its rich green color best with some protection from intense midday sun. Plant in evenly moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil and shelter from drying winter wind. Its congested, sculptural texture makes it a good fit for rock gardens and conifer collections where a slow, textured accent is wanted rather than quick fill-in growth.

common_name: Nana Dwarf Japanese Yew (Low Mounding Rock Garden Yew)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring or fall in moist, well-drained soil; tolerates shade better than almost any other conifer.

directions: This dwarf selection of Japanese yew forms a low, dense, irregularly rounded mound of dark green needles, spreading wider than it grows tall over many decades. It tolerates deep shade better than almost any other conifer, making it useful under trees or on the shaded side of a building where few evergreens thrive, though it also handles full sun if soil moisture is adequate. Grow in moist, well-drained soil and avoid waterlogged sites, which can cause root problems. Female plants produce small red berry-like arils in fall; all plant parts except the aril flesh are toxic if ingested, so site with care around pets and children.

common_name: Repandens Spreading English Yew (Low Wide-Spreading Groundcover Yew)

planting.note: Plant in spring or fall in moist, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun.

directions: Repandens is a low, wide-spreading English yew that stays well under knee height while slowly spreading several feet wide, with branch tips that gracefully droop at their ends. Its dense, dark green, shade-tolerant foliage makes it a durable choice as a tall groundcover, bank cover, or foundation planting beneath windows where a yew's fine texture is wanted without height. Grow in moist, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun, avoiding waterlogged ground. As with other yews, all plant parts except the fleshy red aril are toxic if ingested, so consider placement around pets and children.

common_name: Standishii Golden Irish Yew (Narrow Columnar Dwarf Yew)

planting.note: Plant in spring or fall in moist, well-drained soil; full sun brings out the best gold color.

directions: Standishii is a slow-growing, narrow, upright dwarf yew with golden-yellow foliage, arising as a sport of the columnar Irish yew. Its tight, dense habit and strong vertical line make it useful as a slow-growing accent or narrow hedge element where space is limited, and its color is brightest with good sun exposure. Grow in moist, well-drained soil; it tolerates some shade but turns greener and grows less densely with less light. Like other yews, all parts except the fleshy aril are toxic if ingested, so site thoughtfully around pets and children.

common_name: Nana Dwarf Black Spruce (Compact Blue-Gray Rock Garden Spruce)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in moist, acidic, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade.

directions: This dwarf selection of black spruce forms a dense, slow-growing globe of short, blue-gray needles, staying under two feet tall for many years. It inherits the species' extreme cold hardiness and tolerance of acidic, moisture-retentive soils, making it a reliable choice for rock gardens, trough plantings, and cold-climate containers. Grow in full sun to light shade in evenly moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil, and avoid hot, dry exposures where its boreal origins make it less comfortable than in cooler climates. It needs essentially no pruning, just occasional removal of any reverted, faster-growing shoots to preserve its compact form.

common_name: Holger Juniper (Gold-Tipped Spring Foliage Blue Juniper)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in well-drained soil in full sun for the strongest color contrast.

directions: Holger is a low, mounding juniper whose new spring growth emerges creamy yellow before aging to the steel-blue of its parent, 'Blue Star', creating a two-toned effect across the plant through the growing season. It spreads into a broad, irregular mound of soft, scaly foliage and is well suited to sunny rock gardens, slopes, and mixed borders where its seasonal color shift adds interest beyond typical blue junipers. Grow in full sun and lean, well-drained soil; heavy, wet soils and deep shade both weaken its color and density. Established plants are drought-tolerant and need little maintenance beyond occasional shaping.

common_name: Woodwardii Globe Arborvitae (Dense Rounded Heritage Arborvitae)

planting.note: Plant in spring or fall in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade.

directions: One of the longest-cultivated dwarf arborvitae selections, Woodwardii forms a dense, rounded globe of soft green foliage without the shearing that globe-shaped shrubs usually require. Its naturally tidy, symmetrical habit has made it a dependable foundation and specimen shrub for generations of gardens. Grow in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; foliage can bronze somewhat in harsh winter sun and exposure, recovering with the return of warm weather. It needs little care beyond occasional removal of dead interior growth and protection from heavy snow load, which can splay open its dense branching.

common_name: Minuta Dwarf Hemlock (Extreme Miniature Rock Garden Conifer)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in moist, well-drained, acidic soil in partial shade.

directions: Minuta is one of the smallest named hemlock cultivars, growing into a tight, irregular little bun of fine-textured needles that adds only a sliver of growth each year. Its extreme miniature scale makes it a specialty choice for trough gardens, miniature conifer collections, and alpine-style plantings rather than general landscape use. Grow in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in partial shade, since hemlocks resent hot, dry, or overly sunny sites. It needs essentially no pruning and should be protected from root competition and drought stress, both of which it tolerates poorly given its tiny root system.

common_name: Clanbrassiliana Norway Spruce (Historic Dense Flat-Topped Dwarf Spruce)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade.

directions: Among the oldest named dwarf conifer selections still in cultivation, Clanbrassiliana forms a dense, flat-topped, irregularly rounded mound of short needles that grows extremely slowly even by dwarf spruce standards. Its old-fashioned, gnarled silhouette has long made it a favorite specimen for rock gardens and conifer collections seeking plants with real age and character. Grow in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; plants are generally tough once established but benefit from protection against heavy, wet snow, which can distort the flat crown. Pruning is rarely needed beyond removing occasional dead wood.

planting.note: Plant in spring or fall in moist, well-drained soil in full sun for the densest form.

directions: Hoveyi is a heritage arborvitae selection forming a dense, compact, egg-shaped to rounded bush of bright green foliage, slower growing and more refined in habit than common arborvitae. Its tidy, self-maintaining shape has kept it in cultivation as a foundation and specimen shrub for well over a century. Grow in moist, well-drained soil in full sun; part shade is tolerated but produces looser, less dense growth. It needs minimal pruning beyond removing any fast-growing reverted shoots and benefits from protection against heavy snow load.

common_name: Green Carpet Juniper (Low Mat-Forming Common Juniper)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring in lean, well-drained soil in full sun.

directions: Green Carpet is a very low, flat, mat-forming selection of common juniper, hugging the ground closely while spreading steadily into a dense carpet of fine, bright green needles. It is useful as a true groundcover for sunny banks, rock gardens, and areas where a juniper's toughness is needed but height must stay minimal. Grow in full sun in lean, sharply drained soil; wet, heavy soils invite root and foliage disease. Once established it is quite drought-tolerant and needs little care beyond occasional edging to keep it within bounds.
